Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a logical error in synthesizing the historical data. While the search results correctly identified the "Crossing of the Rhine" as occurring on December 31, 406 (meaning the event happened *at the end* of the year 406), the Planner incorrectly applied a "tie-breaker" rule. The Planner reasoned that because some sources mention a range like "405-406" or "406-407," it should select the *earlier* year (405) to satisfy the "end of which year" phrasing. This is a fundamental misunderstanding of the timeline: the invasion culminated in the year 406, not 405. The event happened *in* 406, specifically at its very end. Selecting 405 contradicts the explicit evidence of the December 31 date found in the search results.
